newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Amnesty condemns Colombia after murders.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty condemns Colombia after murders.

text.p: Amnesty International on Tuesday condemned what it called the Colombian government's failure to protect human rights workers after two respected campaigners were murdered.

Five gunmen smashed their way into a Bogota apartment on Monday and shot dead Mario Calderon and his wife Elsa, who both worked at the Centre for Research and Popular Education (CINEP), a human rights centre run by Jesuit priests.
The CINEP deputy director, Jesuit priest Father Hernan Gonzalez, blamed a right-wing death squad for the murders. There was no word from police who was responsible.

London-based Amnesty said in a statement received here that the Colombian government had "failed on numerous occasions to react to the claims of the military high command, lawmakers and even journalists who have accused human rights workers of being subversives."

"The government has permitted an increase in the number of threats against human rights campaigners which has created an atmosphere in which the dark forces flourish in their desire to carry out these threats," it added.
More than 5,000 human rights activists marched through downtown Bogota on Tuesday protesting against the killings.
Mario Calderon's father-in-law Carlos Alvarado also died in the attack. His mother-in-law suffered bullet wounds but survived, and his 2-year-old son escaped death by hiding in a closet.

Human rights groups say campaigners in Colombia are frequently accused by the military and government officials of being leftist sympathisers and mouthpieces for communist guerrillas who have waged a war against the state for three decades.
